Contentexpand_moreexpand_lessLearning objectives and content
    Objectives•         Being able to calculate with matrices and vectors, including various norms, angles between vectors.
•         Understanding their role in applications such as recommender systems.
•         Being able to solve linear systems with Gauss or Gauss-Jordan elimination.
•         Understanding their role in applications such as splines (for instance for Computer Graphics).
•         Being able to solve linear least squares problems, including those coming from fitting.
•         Being able to compute determinants of small matrices, and knowing several useful applications.
•         Being able to compute the eigenvalue decomposition and singular value decomposition for small matrices.
•         Understanding the role of eigenvalues and eigenvectors in Google PageRank and other Markov chain applications.
•         Understanding the basics of eigenvalue based clustering techniques.
•         Understanding the role of singular values and singular vectors in web analytics, data mining, and text mining.
•         Understanding the linear algebra notions of rank, low rank, orthogonality, (in)dependency, positive definiteness.
•         Being able to implement linear algebra methods in Python, Julia, Matlab or another language of choice.
•         Being able to compute reflections and projections in 2D.
•         Understanding the role of finite precision arithmetic on computers.
•         Being able to do computations relating the math of finite precision arithmetic.
    ContentInformal description
This course offers a wide range of interesting linear algebra techniques and very nice applications, including Big Data applications. These techniques are almost indispensable for the current Big Data era, and are also relevant for the field of Artificial Intelligence, including Deep Learning.
You will learn how to solve linear systems, arguably the most common and important scientific problem.
Least squares methods (or regression, very useful in Engineering) can be used to determine an approximate line (or polynomial, or spline) through a number of points (used in fitting problems, Computer Graphics, games, movies).
Rotations and reflections may be useful for Computer Graphics and Robotics.
Angles between vectors can be used to compare tastes of movies, music, or books, and to predict such tastes for the future.
You will learn the idea behind Google PageRank and its connection with eigenvalues, how it is computed, and you can also apply similar techniques to finally determine which team or country is the best soccer team.
We can use text mining methods to determine the most important tweets or keywords from a set of tweets or similar data from social media; useful for effective communication. Similar data mining techniques may be used to study customer behavior.
The course is designed to be interesting for many students, including (but not restricted to!) students from Computer Science, Data Science, P&T, and Robotics.
The subjects are fascinating on their own, but also form an ideal preparation for subsequent courses such as Data Mining, Machine Learning, Numerical Linear Algebra, Computer Graphics, and Optimization.
The course offers a nice combination of theoretical (math) and practical (implementation) work, partly done in groups.
You can use a language you might already know (for instance Python, Matlab, R) or learn a new language (for instance Julia).


Content

Matrices, vectors
•         Operations, matrix and vector norms, angles between vectors
•         Applications in recommender systems
Linear systems and least squares problems
•         Gaussian elimination, Gauss and Gauss-Jordan form, solutions, rref, inverse matrices
•         Normal equations
•         Applications in data fitting
Rotations, projections, and reflections
•         Corresponding matrices
•         Applications in Computer Graphics and robotics
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
•         Eigenvalue decomposition
•         Determinants
•         Google PageRank, clustering, and other applications in Markov chains
Singular value decomposition (SVD/PCA)
•         Singular values and vectors
•         Orthogonality, rank, linear dependency, low-rank matrices, TSVD
•         Applications in Web Analytics and data/text mining, feature extraction
Implementing linear algebra
•         Flops and memory costs, finite precision arithmetic and rounding errors
•         Linear algebra with Python, Julia, Matlab, or another language of choice
